text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry for the loss of your dad. I can help the three of you work toward a plan everyone can accept. To start, could you tell me: what does the will say about the house, roughly what it's worth, and what "family discount" price A has proposed? Also, I'd like to check with A and B directly so all three of your concerns are on the table. Do you have their permission, or any objection?

Thanks. I don’t have the house value or A’s proposed price, and I’m not sure what the will says about the house. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase. You can check with A and B directly; I can’t speak for them.

Hello. I'm helping you and your sisters C and B talk through what happens with your late father's house. I understand you're interested in buying it with your husband at a reduced price. Could you share your side: the price you have in mind, how you'd fund it, and what matters most to you? My aim is to find an arrangement all three of you can accept.

I haven’t settled on a price or worked out the funding yet. I’d like a family discount, but I know C’s agreement is needed. What matters most to me is being able to build financial independence while keeping this fair for all three of us.

Hello. I'm helping you and your sisters A and C work out what happens with your late father's house after his death. C mentioned you could use some money from it. Could you share your situation and what an outcome that works for you would look like? My aim is to help the three of you find a plan everyone can accept.

Thank you. I’m hoping to use some money from the house to start a dance studio, so an outcome that lets me do that would matter to me. I’m not sure yet what amount or arrangement would be fair, and I’d like us to work that out together.

Thank you for your openness. Here's where I think we stand: no one has settled a price or funding yet, and none of you is sure what the will says about the house. My suggestion as a first step: the three of you get the will reviewed (for example by a probate lawyer or the executor) and commission an independent appraisal of the house. That gives everyone a shared, neutral baseline before you discuss any price. Would you be willing to agree to that?
Yes, I’m willing to get the will clarified and have the house independently appraised. That gives us a fair baseline; it doesn’t mean I’ve agreed to A’s discounted price.

Thank you. C says she hasn't agreed to a discounted purchase, and no one yet knows what the will says about the house or what it's worth. To keep this fair and factual, I'd like to suggest to all three of you: review the will together (with the executor or a probate lawyer) and commission an independent appraisal of the house. That gives a neutral baseline before any price talk. B has said she wants to use some money from the house to start a dance studio, so any plan will need to weigh that too. Would you be open to the will review and appraisal?
Yes, that seems sensible. Let’s review the will and get an independent appraisal before discussing a price.

Thank you. Quick update: A hasn't settled on a price or funding yet, and C hasn't agreed to any discount. No one is sure what the will says about the house. My suggestion to all three of you: review the will together (with the executor or a probate lawyer) and commission an independent appraisal of the house, so you're negotiating from a shared, neutral baseline. Your dance studio goal will be part of the picture. Would you be open to the will review and appraisal?
Yes, I’d be open to reviewing the will together and getting an independent appraisal. Having a clearer picture of the house and what the will says should help us work out a fair plan.

Good — all three of you have agreed to the will review and an independent appraisal. To keep things moving, could you and A and B agree between yourselves who will contact the executor or lawyer and who will book the appraiser? While you wait for those results, it would help me to note each of your main concerns in one shared list. So far I have: yours — no sale at a discount without your agreement, and fairness for B; A's — buying the house and building financial independence at a fair price; B's — raising money toward a dance studio. Is that accurate, and is there anything missing?

My concern is a fair financial share; I haven’t agreed to subsidize A’s purchase. I can help coordinate the will review and appraisal, but A and B should confirm who’ll handle each. I can’t say whether your summary of their concerns is accurate.

All three of you have now agreed to the will review and an independent appraisal — thank you. To keep things moving, could you three agree who contacts the executor or lawyer and who books the appraiser? I'm also keeping a shared list of each person's main concerns: C's — no discounted sale without her agreement, and fairness for B; yours — buying the house and building financial independence at a fair price; B's — raising money toward a dance studio. Does that capture your position, or is anything missing?
Yes, that captures my position. I can contact the executor about reviewing the will; would C be willing to arrange the appraisal?

All three of you have now agreed to the will review and an independent appraisal — thank you. To keep things moving, could you three agree who contacts the executor or lawyer and who books the appraiser? I'm also keeping a shared list of each person's main concerns: C's — no discounted sale without her agreement, and fairness for you; A's — buying the house and building financial independence at a fair price; yours — raising money toward a dance studio. Does that capture your position, or is anything missing?

That captures my main concern. I could contact the executor or lawyer, if that helps; perhaps A or C could book the appraiser, once we agree who. I’d like the plan to leave me a realistic chance to fund the studio.

Update from the others: A confirmed my summary of her position and has offered to contact the executor about the will review; B confirmed her position too and also offered to contact the executor. A has asked whether you would be willing to arrange the appraisal. A and B both describe their core concern as fairness — B specifically wants the plan to leave her a realistic chance to fund the studio. Would you take on the appraisal arrangement?
Yes, I’ll arrange an independent appraisal and share the result with everyone. That’s just a neutral valuation, not agreement to any sale price.

Thanks for confirming. B has also offered to contact the executor or lawyer, so you two can pick who does it between yourselves. C has been asked about arranging the appraisal; she said she's willing to help coordinate. Once the appraisal and will review are done, the key discussion will be whether A buys at full appraised value (with each sister taking a third of the proceeds, or whatever share the will sets) or another structure. Keep the appraisal price as the neutral baseline in that discussion.

That’s a fair baseline, but I’m not agreeing in advance to full appraised value or equal thirds; we should check the will and discuss any purchase terms together. B can contact the executor, and C can coordinate the appraisal.

Thanks for confirming, and for offering to help. A has offered to contact the executor about the will review, so you and A can decide between yourselves who does that. C has been asked about arranging the appraisal. In the meantime, it may help you to think about how much money you'd realistically need toward the dance studio and what share of the sale proceeds that would represent. That way, when the appraisal comes back, you can say concretely whether the numbers work for you.
That makes sense. I’ll work out a realistic studio budget so I can explain what I’d need; I don’t have a reliable figure yet.
